$comment: Export projection for a tenant site.db, version 2 (schema v3). The unit of reproducibility is this projection, not the file: two VACUUM INTO copies of the same logical content are not byte-identical once any volatile table has a row (scripts/model/verify_claims.py check 16). 'rows' = data travels; 'empty' = the table exists in the bundle and carries no rows; 'filtered' = rows travel subject to the SQL predicate in `filter`. C-5: the completeness rule is a UNION evaluated against the live database, not a set difference over one file — set(sqlite_master) == core_tables (this file) + u_* tables (prefix rule, class rows) + p_<id>_* tables (class from the installed manifest's tables[].export). A table present in the database and absent from all three is a build failure; a plugin table whose manifest declares no export class is refused at install with SKW_E_PL_NO_EXPORT_CLASS.

u_.why: Tenant-built tables are the tenant's content. They are not named here because their names are not knowable at build time; the class is a fact of the prefix (register §4.2). A u_* table's rows travel, its DDL is already in the file.

p_.why: A plugin table's class is decided by the publisher and reviewed at install, then read from cms_plugin_installed.manifest_json.tables[].export. 'manifest' is not a fourth class: it resolves to one of the three, and an absent or unknown value is a refusal.

cms_settings.filter: key NOT GLOB 'demo.*' AND key NOT GLOB 'billing.*'
cms_settings.why: Site configuration travels; operator-only namespaces (demo furniture, billing state) do not. Without the filter a bundle exported from a demo goes live wearing the demo banner and noindex tag (Red Team O2).

cms_component_registry.why: The page bodies in this bundle are written in this registry's vocabulary. The image re-upserts its own components at boot, but the rows make the bundle self-describing and let install.sh refuse a bundle whose pages name a component the image does not have.

cms_page_revision.why: The undo history is part of the handover: the client's first action after install is usually to fix a typo we made.

cms_nav.why: The site is unusable without its navigation.

cms_asset.why: Media library. Gated rows are refused by the exporter before this projection is applied (SKW_E_EXP_GATED_ASSETS).

cms_asset_alias.why: Old keys must still 301 inside the client's instance, or every URL we ever published to them dies at handover.

cms_asset_variant.why: Derived files, but the rows are the index of which files exist; regenerating them all on install is minutes of CPU on a box we do not control.

cms_asset_link.why: The usage graph; without it 'delete this image' stops warning about the page that uses it.

cms_asset_bundle.why: A sellable set is content, not commerce state.

cms_download_code.why: Purchaser emails, order refs and live code fingerprints. A sold bundle has no issuers and no buyers; carrying the rows hands the client our customer list and our live codes (Red Team O3).

cms_download_code_archive.why: Accounting for events we pruned. It is our reconciliation evidence, not the client's content, and v1 never prunes so the table is empty by construction.

cms_download_event.why: ip_hash/ua_hash are personal data collected for our forensics, and the rows are per-request volatile, so they break reproduction as well.

cms_watermark_render.why: One stamped file per purchaser, each carrying a different buyer's email. It is the single largest PII store in the file and the one that grows without bound (Red Team O12). C-16 also excludes the files themselves from every target.

cms_form.why: Form definitions are part of the site.

cms_form_submission.why: Prospect PII from our sales pipeline, not the client's content (Red Team O3). A CMS sold to the same client can export with --include-pii, which is an explicit operator decision with an audit row.

cms_datasource.why: The site's data bindings; a page whose source is missing renders an empty region.

cms_view_registry.why: Views are migration-owned and the DDL postcondition reads this table; a bundle without it fails its own integrity check.

cms_table_registry.why: The u_* inventory. EXPORT-NOTES.md must state its row count and BUNDLE.json carries source_counts.

cms_trigger_registry.why: C-5: the DDL postcondition reads it ('every trigger is in this registry'), so a bundle without the rows fails verification on the client's box. It was the table the old static-file check could not see.

cms_audit.why: Our operators' actions and labels. The client starts with an empty audit log, which is honest: we did not do anything on their box yet. The chain's head is sealed in the source install's control.db, not shipped.

cms_css_blob.why: The stylesheet a document names by hash. Drop it and every page in the bundle links a file that is not there — the site arrives unstyled, which is a worse handover than one that arrives slightly dated.

cms_theme.why: The uploaded looks travel with the site, including the active one: a client who receives a site wearing a theme we uploaded must be able to see, keep and re-activate it.

cms_redirect.why: Redirects are content; dropping them 404s every slug we renamed during the build.

cms_plugin_installed.why: A bundle carries the plugin: code reference, signature state, root hash and above all the manifest, which is the only source of its p_* tables' export classes (C-5).

cms_plugin_migration.why: The bundle's site.db already contains the plugin's tables; without the ledger the first enable would try to re-apply forward-only migrations.

cms_plugin_setting.why: O-44: a secret setting must never leave the install. The row stays so the plugin knows the key exists and needs a value; the value does not travel, and the install screen asks for it.

cms_plugin_revoked.why: C-9: revocation is local to the install. Carrying our revocation list to a client would leak our trust decisions and could not be enforced on their box anyway.
